To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transonic flow over a boattailed body is strongly interacting, and the potential flow theory is not sufficient.
the boattail afterbody is the best configuration for transonic flow and that the boattailed afterbodies have a very strong interaction with the transonic flow.
the boattailed afterbodies are very effective in reducing wave drag and the full potential equation should be considered in the analysis of the transonic boattail flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical solution of the full potential equation in the presence of transonic flow.
the numerical study of transonic flow over boattailed afterbodies.
the development of an accurate, efficient, and reliable computational method for predicting transonic flow about boattailed afterbodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the boattail is not a simple afterbody.
the transonic flow over boattails is strongly influenced by the afterbody geometry.
the transonic flow over boattailed afterbodies is strongly interactive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transonic flow field around a boattailed configuration can be described by a potential flow solution with a small perturbation of a strong interaction character.
a boattail can reduce the pressure drag of a body in subsonic and transonic regimes, and that the boattail can also reduce the pressure drag in a supersonic regime.
the boattail is not an afterbody which may be added to a body of revolution to improve the drag characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transonic flow around boattailed afterbodies can be predicted accurately with a potential flow model.
a strong interaction can be expected when the boattail is sufficiently slender and the Mach number is sufficiently high.
the transonic flow field is highly three-dimensional and the flow is strongly influenced by the geometry of the boattail.
